chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him—informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a mouse falling into the well. He said: “Seven buckets.”
He said: And I asked him about a bird and a chicken falling into the well. He said: “Seven buckets; and for the cat, twenty or thirty or forty buckets; and the dog and whatever resembles it.”

His statement عليه السلام, “and the dog and whatever resembles it,” means in accordance with its bodily size. This includes the sheep, the gazelle, the fox, the pig, and everything mentioned, and this is also indicated by it.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed for purification
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse that falls into the well
key_terms.دَلْوًا: a bucket used for drawing water from the well
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets to be drawn from the well
key_terms.شِبْهُهُ: whatever resembles it in bodily size or category

ai.seo_question: How many buckets must be drawn from a well when a mouse, bird, cat, or dog falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the purification of well water when certain animals fall into it. It specifies the number of buckets to be drawn in different cases and includes a clarification that animals similar to the dog are treated according to their bodily size.
